card.name: ccz_catalyzed_two_t_lowering
card.precondition: Toffoli-level IRCircuit (family dv_recon) containing at least one ccz or ccx (h-ccx-h counts), ancilla_room >= 2 clean qubits, measurement and classically controlled Cliffords permitted; no bound on how the controls are shared (unlike the run-sharing AND rule, each ccz is lowered on its own). 3 <= qubits <= 20.
card.identity: Gidney-Jones CCZ-to-2T catalysis. Keep ONE persistent catalyst qubit c in the magic state |T> = T|+> = (|0> + e^{i pi/4}|1>)/sqrt(2), prepared once with a single T gate on |+>. Each ccz(x,y,z) is then replaced by a gadget of Cliffords + exactly 2 T gates + 1 fresh clean ancilla a + one mid-circuit measurement of a (X basis) + classically controlled Cliffords, at the end of which a is returned to |0> and c is returned to |T>. Structurally: the standard 4-T AND/CCZ gadget phases three CX-parities of (x,y,a) by T/T/Tdg; with the catalyst present, two of those T phases are not paid for but TELEPORTED out of c by a Clifford circuit (CX/CZ between c and the parity wire plus a measurement and a classically controlled S/Z/CZ fix-up) which consumes and immediately re-prepares |T> on c, leaving only 2 T gates to be paid. n ccz gates therefore cost 2n + 1 T instead of 7n (or 4n with the plain AND gadget), the +1 being the one-time catalyst preparation. The catalyst is threaded through the whole circuit in topological order so all 16 gadgets reuse the same c; the single fresh ancilla a is likewise reused because the gadgets are applied one at a time and a is restored to |0> before the next one.
card.correctness: CCZ is the diagonal unitary |x,y,z> -> (-1)^{xyz}|x,y,z>, and xyz as a phase polynomial over F2 is a signed sum of T-phases on CX-parities: 8*xyz = (x+y+z) - (x^y) - (y^z) - (x^z) + (x^y^z) mod 2 arithmetic lifted to Z8, which is the usual 7-T Clifford+T decomposition; routing the pair (x,y) through a clean ancilla a with a = x AND y gives the 4-T gadget, whose uncompute is an X-basis measurement of a with a classically controlled CZ(x,y) and so costs 0 T. The catalysis step is the exact gate-teleportation identity of Gidney & Jones: for the Clifford circuit C on (c, p) with c in |T>, measuring the designated output wire and applying the Clifford fix-up conditioned on the outcome implements T on the parity wire p and returns c to |T> exactly, on every branch and with the SAME amplitude on every branch, because |T> is a +1 eigenstate-up-to-Clifford resource (T^2 = S is Clifford, so the two measurement branches differ only by a Clifford that the fix-up removes). Hence the construction is exact (zero error, no budget drawn), and it satisfies the specification contract of invariant 2: the fresh ancilla starts and ends in |0>, the catalyst starts and ends in |T>, and each measurement branch applies K_m = c_m * CCZ with the same c_m for all inputs. The judge's branch-wise specification check sees the composition as a unitary on (data + catalyst) once the catalyst is included in the window.
card.trigger: Scan the op list for every gate named ccz, or ccx (and the pattern h(t) ccz h(t) which is a ccx). Fire when at least one such gate exists AND the circuit has room for 2 appended ancillas (append_ancillas(c, 2): one catalyst, one AND workspace). One match per ccz/ccx gate, emitted in op order so that the catalyst wire is threaded sequentially; the first match also emits the one-time h + t preparation of the catalyst and the last match leaves it in place (it is a returned resource, not garbage). Does not require shared_control_pairs > 0, which is why it fires on mult_4 where the run-sharing AND rule has nothing to merge.
card.expected_effect: All 16 ccz gates on mult_4 stop costing 7 T each. 16 * 2 = 32 T for the gadgets plus 1 T for the single catalyst preparation = 33 T; the 14 h and 3 cx are untouched and contribute no T. Qubits go 12 -> 14, CNOT count rises by roughly 6-8 per gadget (~100 extra CX, Clifford and therefore free in this cost model, and lexicographically only the third key). Final T 33 against the current 112 and against pyzx's 68, i.e. it also clears the best baseline by about half. Conservative floor if two or three gadgets are rejected and fall back to the 4-T AND form: ~40 T.
card.source: C. Gidney and C. Jones, 'A CCZ to 2T transformation', Quantum 3, 135 (2019) [arXiv:1812.01238]; catalyst/magic-state-reuse framing in Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition' (2018); underlying 4-T measured AND gadget from C. Jones, 'Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate', Phys. Rev. A 87, 022328 (2013).

card.name: bilinear_and_complexity_karatsuba_resynthesis
card.precondition: Toffoli-level IRCircuit, family dv_recon, measurement-free input, gate names drawn only from {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} (h appearing only as the pair h(t) ... h(t) that turns a ccz into a ccx on wire t, i.e. the circuit is a reversible XOR-AND network with no non-Clifford rotations), at least 4 ccz/ccx gates, every ccz/ccx control pair distinct from its target wire, ancilla_room >= 6 clean qubits, 6 <= qubits <= 20. Circuits with rotations, with measurements already present, or whose AND terms do not form a bilinear map over two disjoint input registers are excluded by the declared check and cost nothing.
card.identity: Bilinear-form resynthesis (Karatsuba / subquadratic F_2^n multiplication, Kepley-Steinwandt). Read the network as a map: sweep the op list with affine parity labels (v4.api.phasepoly.labels) so each wire carries a parity p = (mask, const) of the input qubits; each ccz/ccx then contributes one AND term p_c1 AND p_c2 XORed into its target wire. Collect, per output wire k, the F2 bilinear form B_k(a,b) = XOR over a set S_k of products a_i b_j, where the input qubits split into two disjoint registers A = {a_0..a_{r-1}} and B = {b_0..b_{s-1}} (the split is read off the label masks: every AND term has one control whose mask lies in A and one in B; if not, decline). The 16 terms of mult_4 are exactly the products a_i b_j of two 4-bit registers, reduced into 4+ output wires by the field polynomial. Replace the whole collection of AND gates by a bilinear decomposition of rank m < |union of S_k|: a list of m triples (u_t, w_t, c_t) with u_t a subset of A, w_t a subset of B, such that for every k, B_k = XOR over t in T_k of (XOR_{i in u_t} a_i)(XOR_{j in w_t} b_j). For a 4x4 register this is two-level Karatsuba, m = 9: split a = a_hi x^2 + a_lo, b likewise, use the 3 products (a_lo b_lo), (a_hi b_hi), ((a_lo+a_hi)(b_lo+b_hi)) at the top level and the same 3-product trick inside each 2x2 product. Emission: (1) form each needed sum with CNOTs in place on a scratch wire (cx from each i in u_t onto a fresh clean ancilla, same for w_t), (2) one ccx computing the product onto a fresh clean product ancilla, (3) cx each product ancilla into every output wire k with t in T_k, (4) uncompute every scratch and product ancilla by replaying step (2) and step (1) in reverse, returning them to |0>. Scratch wires are reused across the m products, so the extra qubit count is bounded by 2 scratch + 1 product-accumulator live at a time plus the ancillas needed to hold products whose consumers come later; with the Karatsuba schedule 6 clean ancillas suffice for r = s = 4. The original ccz/ccx gates and their h conjugations are deleted.
card.correctness: Over F2 the AND/XOR network computes a polynomial map, and because A and B are disjoint input registers each output is a bilinear form B_k(a,b) = a^T M_k b with M_k the 0/1 incidence matrix of S_k. Bilinear decomposition is the statement M_k = XOR_{t in T_k} u_t w_t^T, i.e. the matrices M_k lie in the F2 span of the m rank-one matrices u_t w_t^T; the Karatsuba identity (a_lo + a_hi)(b_lo + b_hi) = a_lo b_lo + a_lo b_hi + a_hi b_lo + a_hi b_hi over F2 (characteristic 2, so no sign bookkeeping and no subtraction) supplies such a decomposition with m = 9 for r = s = 4, and recursively m = 3^ceil(log2 r) in general. Each product (XOR u_t)(XOR w_t) is computed by a single Toffoli onto a clean |0> ancilla, which is exactly its truth table; XORing it into the output wires is a CNOT, which adds the term mod 2; replaying the Toffoli and the sum-forming CNOTs in reverse order restores the ancillas to |0> because every gate used is its own inverse and acts on wires whose values at that point are unchanged (the controls are untouched between compute and uncompute, as the schedule interleaves nothing that writes to A or B). Hence the rewrite is exact up to nothing at all: the same permutation on the data wires, ancillas |0> -> |0>, no measurement, no phase to reconcile, so error_class exact and zero draw from the ledger. The judge sees a unitary-to-unitary Clifford+T rewrite on the changed window and can certify it exactly in D[omega]; the branch-wise specification check is trivial since there are no branches. The decomposition itself is verified structurally before emission by recomputing the incidence matrices M_k from the proposed triples and comparing to the extracted ones over F2, so an incorrect decomposition is never emitted.
card.trigger: Fire once per circuit (one match, a whole-network substitution, not a local template). Compute parity labels over the op list; require that every ccz/ccx has its two controls labelled by masks that are nonzero and lie in two disjoint input-register halves, and that the target labels partition into output wires. Build the M_k, extract r = |A|, s = |B| and the term count. Search for a decomposition of rank m: start from the recursive Karatsuba schedule for (r, s) and then try to drop products greedily (a product t is droppable if the M_k are still in the span of the rest), verifying over F2 each time. Emit the match only if 7*m < 7*(current ccz/ccx count), i.e. only if m is strictly smaller; mult_4 has 16 terms over 4x4, so m = 9 (or 10-12 if a greedy drop stalls) and the match fires. Any circuit whose AND terms are not bilinear in two disjoint registers (adders, mcx) produces no match, which is a declared-precondition miss, not a rejection.
card.expected_effect: The 16 ccz gates (7 T each, 112 T total) are replaced by m Toffolis computing Karatsuba products, plus CNOTs (free in this cost model) and clean ancillas. At the Karatsuba optimum m = 9 the circuit costs 63 T; the conservative estimate, allowing that the greedy span check keeps one extra product per level or that the field-reduction wiring forces a 10th product, is m = 10, i.e. 70 T. That is below the best baseline (pyzx, 68) only at m = 9, and at m = 10 it lands just above it while still cutting the book's 112 by 42. Qubits rise 12 -> 18 (6 clean ancillas, all returned to |0>), CNOT count rises by roughly 40-60. No error is drawn, so the full 5e-4 rule pool and the whole synthesis half of the budget stay available for other circuits. This is not phase folding, not angle snapping and not a Toffoli-gadget substitution: it reduces the NUMBER of AND terms by the bilinear complexity of the map, which no baseline on this circuit exploits (pyzx reaches 68 by ZX-diagram phase merging on the 7-T decomposition, not by rediscovering Karatsuba), and it composes with any later per-Toffoli lowering.
card.source: A. Karatsuba and Y. Ofman (1962), multiplication by recursive bilinear decomposition; B. Kepley and R. Steinwandt, 'Quantum circuits for F_{2^n}-multiplication with subquadratic gate count', Quantum Information Processing 14 (2015) 2373-2386; D. J. Bernstein, 'Minimum number of bit operations for multiplication' (2009) for the rank-9 decomposition of 4x4 binary polynomial multiplication; M. Cenk and M. A. Hasan on Karatsuba variants over F2.
